full_judgment: This appeal at the instance of the 5 defendants, sons of Munshi Sohrab Ali, is directed against the judgment and decree of the learned District Judge modifying the judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Noakhali in Partition Suit No. 54 of 1966. The plaintiff brought a suit for partition of property Nos. 1 and 2 of the schedule attached to the plaint and their case was that property No. 1 belonged to his mother Arfarunnessa who died leaving the plaintiff Sadu Mia and his brother Nadu Mia as two sons and Ambia Khatun and Mahmuda Khatun as two daughters and plaintiffs father Nasir Ali to inherit her said property. Plaintiffs' father Nasir Ali also died and thereafter died his sister and brother Nadu Mia, leaving the plaintiff to inherit 12 annas share of his mother's property No.1, measuring an area of 2.29 acres of land Plaintiffs further case was that his father Nasir Ali took a second wife after the death of the plaintiffs mother and defendant Nos. 1 and 2, were the sons of Nasir Ali by his second wife. As to property No. 2 of the plaint it was the plaintiffs case that Nabijan Bibi, predecessor of defendant Nos. 3-10 had 3 annas 10 gandas share in the said property. Nasir Ali, father of the plaintiff, had 4 annas 10 gandas share and plaintiff’s sisters Ambia Khatun and Mahmuda Khatun had 1 anna 6 gandas 2 Karas and 2 Krantis share each, while the plaintiff and his brother Nadu Mia had 2 annas 13 gandas 1 Kara 1 Kranti share each. After the death of his father, brother and sisters the plaintiff inherited the interest of his brothers and sisters in property No. 2 and also l/3rd share of his father but as the property was not partitioned by metes and bounds he asked partition from the defendants but having failed he had filed the suit for a partition. The suit was contested by defendant Nos. 39 and 40 by filing a joint written statement and also by defendant Nos. 18, 20, 22, 23, 34 in a group by filing a joint written statement. Defendant Nos. 18, 19, 20, 23 and 34 are the transferees from other defendants and they claimed to be in possession of the suit land. The case of defendant Nos. 39 and 40 was that the plaintiff’s father Nasir Ali sold his 8 annas share in the suit land on behalf of himself and his minor children including the plaintiff to defendant Nos. 28 and 29 for legal necessity by a registered kabala dated 20th Baisak, 1324 BS (Ext. A) and that the plaintiff never challenged that kabala on attaining majority and they cannot now question that sale. It is their further case that after the said sale, plaintiffs father Nasir Ali took lease of 10 ganda of land from that property by executing a registered kabuliyat, dated 4th Ashar, 1324 BS (Ext. Dl). Their further case was that the remaining half of the suit raiyati was auction purchased by the original landlord Rokeya Bibi in Rent Execution Case No. 298 of 1913 and she leased out the same to defendant Nos. 39 and 40 by executing a registered patta, dated 27th Falgun, 1324 BS (Ext. B) after which Nasir Ali, plaintiffs father, executed a registered nadabi deed, dated 13th Chaitra, 1323 BS (Ext. C) and then took lease of 9 gandas of the same by executing a registered kabuliyat, dated 4th Chaitra, 1324 BS (Ext. D). Thus excepting 9 gandas of Nasir Ali's leasehok tenancy the remaining of the property of property Nos. 1 and 2 came to the ownership of defendant Nos. 28, 29, 39 and 40. It was their further case that even the 10 gandas of the land leased out to Nasir Ali for a jam a of Tk. 5.00 was auction sold and purchased by defendant Nos. 28, 29, on 1935 AD after which the plaintiffs themselves took lease of that land by executing a kabuliyat in 1348 BS (Ext. D2) but in spite of the settlement by Rokeya in favour of the defendants vide (Ext. B) the names of the defendants were not recorded in the CS Khatian which was wrong; Their further case was that they have thereafter sold their interest in the suit land to defendant Nos. 14, 18, 19, 22, 23, 24, 32 to 36 by different registered kabalas on different dates and hence the plaintiffs suit is liable to be dismissed.
